Use this sheet with [the exercise](exercise-student.html). Predict before reading the results, then explain in words. These figures use exact updating or supplied fits, with no new Stan inference.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(posterior)
library(here)
source(here("R/functions.R"))
source(here("R/course_data.R"))
source(here("R/course_utils.R"))
source(here("R/course_visuals.R"))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE,fig.width=8,fig.height=4.5)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size=14))
```

## The core comparisons

```{r comparisons}
plot_update(2,5,1,1)
plot_update(40,100,1,1)
plot_update(2,5,8,2)
cases <- tribble(~y,~N,~a,~b, 2,5,1,1, 40,100,1,1, 2,5,8,2)
knitr::kable(pmap_dfr(cases,summarise_update),digits=3)
```

The first two cases fix the prior and observed proportion. The first and third fix
the data. More data narrow this posterior. A high-survival prior moves the small-data
posterior towards higher values. The prior needs ecological justification.

## Stan demonstration

```{r stan-result}
fit <- course_fit("day1_seedling")
knitr::kable(course_diagnostics(fit),digits=2)
ggplot(as_tibble(fit$draws),aes(p))+geom_histogram(bins=30,fill="#d95f02")+
  labs(x="Survival probability",y="Posterior draws")
```

This is the 2/5, Beta(1,1) posterior. Stored draws approximate a distribution.
